<header class="dg-head dg-head-section"><p class="dg-kicker">Chapter 9 <span class="dg-sep">•</span> <a href="index.html">Newton-Cartan Theory</a></p><h1 class="dg-title"><span class="dg-secnum">9.1</span> Newtonian Spacetime</h1></header>
<ul class="dg-itemize dg-depth-1">
<li><p>Given a 4-dimensional smooth manifold <span class="math inline">\((\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{O}, \mathcal{A})\)</span>, an <strong>absolute time</strong> is a scalar field  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            t \colon \mathcal{M} &amp;\longrightarrow \mathbb{R} \\
            p                    &amp;\longmapsto t(p),
        \end{align*}</span>  <span class="math inline">\(t \in C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\)</span>, such that <span class="math inline">\((dt)_p \neq 0\)</span> <span class="math inline">\(\forall p \in \mathcal{M}\)</span>. It assigns to every event the universal time at which it happens, as Newtonian physics assumes, and the condition <span class="math inline">\((dt)_p \neq 0\)</span> ensures that time never stands still; at every event there are directions along which <span class="math inline">\(t\)</span> increases.</p></li>
<li><p>The <strong>absolute space</strong> at time <span class="math inline">\(\tau \in t(\mathcal{M})\)</span> is the level set  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            \mathcal{S}_\tau \coloneqq \mathrm{preim}_t(\{\tau\})
            \longrightarrow
            \mathcal{M} = \dot{\bigcup}_{\tau \in t(\mathcal{M})} \mathcal{S}_\tau,
        \end{align*}</span>  i.e. the set of all events simultaneous at time <span class="math inline">\(\tau\)</span>. Since <span class="math inline">\((dt)_p \neq 0\)</span>, each <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{S}_\tau\)</span> is a 3-dimensional smooth submanifold with <span class="math inline">\(T_p\mathcal{S}_{t(p)}\)</span>, of dimension <span class="math inline">\(3\)</span>. The absolute spaces thus foliate <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{M}\)</span> into copies of “space at a given instant”, and simultaneity is absolute (it does not depend on any observer).</p></li>
<li><p>Given a connection <span class="math inline">\(\nabla\)</span>, absolute time <strong>flows uniformly</strong> if  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            \nabla_{\mathcal{X}} dt = 0, \quad \forall \mathcal{X} \in \Gamma T\mathcal{M},\quad \mathrm{compactly\, written\ as}\quad \nabla dt = 0.
        \end{align*}</span></p></li>
<li><p>A <strong>Newtonian spacetime</strong> is the quintuple <span class="math inline">\((\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{O}, \mathcal{A}, \nabla, t)\)</span> formed by a 4-dimensional torsion-free<sup class="dg-fnref"><a href="#fn-1" id="fnref-1" aria-label="Footnote 1">1</a></sup> affine manifold <span class="math inline">\((\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{O}, \mathcal{A}, \nabla)\)</span> equipped with an absolute time <span class="math inline">\(t\)</span> which flows uniformly. Note that no notion of spatial distance enters these axioms, Newtonian gravity can be described by <span class="math inline">\(\nabla\)</span> alone<sup class="dg-fnref"><a href="#fn-2" id="fnref-2" aria-label="Footnote 2">2</a></sup>.</p></li>
</ul>
<div class="dg-footnotes"><div class="dg-fn" id="fn-1"><a class="dg-fn-num" href="#fnref-1" aria-label="Back to the text">1</a><div class="dg-fn-body"><p>Free particles only measure the symmetric part <span class="math inline">\(\Gamma^k_{(ji)}\)</span>, through the autoparallel equation, so Newton’s axioms leave torsion undetermined. Setting it to zero selects the unique connection fixed by free particles, the only one whose curvature depends on observable quantities alone. Torsion would still affect the parallel transport of other vectors, and becomes observable once these are given physical meaning, e.g. through gyroscopes or a compatible spatial metric (Appendix <a class="dg-xref" href="../proofs-and-additional-material/torsion-newton.html" data-kind="section" data-label="section_Torsion_Newton">B.22</a>).</p></div></div><div class="dg-fn" id="fn-2"><a class="dg-fn-num" href="#fnref-2" aria-label="Back to the text">2</a><div class="dg-fn-body"><p>The relation of this formulation to alternative geometric formulations of Newtonian gravity, is discussed in Appendix <span class="dg-xref dg-xref-pending" data-label="section_Newtonian_Formulations">B.21</span>.</p></div></div></div>
